review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–61). It contains one declaration, `NoncollapsedRCD.regular_good_coordinate_sets`. Its conclusion is an existential statement with many conjuncts: ∃ t s, 0 < t ∧ 0 < s ∧ ∀ R, … ∃ u v U, … ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, …. A statement of this shape is not an equation or iff, so it cannot serve as a rewrite rule. Marking it `@[simp]` would not make sense. The file defines no functions, structures or abbreviations, so there are no definitional unfolding or projection simp lemmas that could be missing. The proof never calls `simp`, `simp only`, `simp_all` or `norm_num [..]` with simp sets. It uses `obtain`/`refine`, `min_le_left`/`min_le_right`, `le_div_iff₀`, `positivity`, `linarith only` and `nlinarith only`, and finishes with `mono_error` on the earlier coordinate result. As a result, the file has no rewrite direction, competing rules, unwanted expansion or rewrite cycle to assess. I searched the repository for uses of the theorem name. The only match outside this file is a similarly named but separate declaration, `regular_good_coordinate_sets_bounded`, in RegularGoodCoordinateSetsBounded.lean. Nothing calls this theorem through simp. The simp-interface rubric therefore has no suitable target in this file.
